<!-- theorem-1: body_md -->
\label{thm: main}
    All 3-IETs are spectrally disjoint from every mixing system. In particular, there is no 3-IET which has a Lebesgue component in its spectrum.
<!-- end theorem-1 -->
<!-- theorem-2: body_md -->
\label{thm:main2}
    All 3-IETs are disjoint in the sense of Furstenberg from all lightly mixing systems. In particular, none of the 3-IETs has a lightly mixing factor.
<!-- end theorem-2 -->
<!-- lemma-1: body_md -->
\label{lem: criterium}
Let $(X,\mu,T)$ be such that there exists an increasing sequence $(n_k)_{k=1}^{\infty}$ for which we have
\[
U_T^{-n_k}\to P(U_T)\quad \text{on}\quad L^2_0(X,\mu)
\]
in the weak operator topology, where $P:\mathbb C\to \mathbb C$ is a non-zero Laurent polynomial. 
Then $T$ is spectrally disjoint from all mixing systems.
<!-- end lemma-1 -->
<!-- theorem-3: body_md -->
\label{thm: operator_limits}
Let $S$ be an ergodic $\mu$-measure preserving Borel automorphism of a compact metric space $(X,d)$. Let also $f:X\to\mathbb{Z}_+$. Assume that there exists a sequence $(q_n)_{n=1}^{\infty}$ such that 
\begin{equation}\label{eq: rigidity}
\sup_{x\in X}\,d(S^{q_n}x,x)\to 0\quad\text{as}\ n\to\infty.
\end{equation}
Assume also that there exists an increasing integer sequence $(h_n)_{n=1}^{\infty}$ such that
\begin{equation}\label{eq: BSconvergence}
\lim_{n\to\infty}(\sum_{k=0}^{q_n-1}f\circ S^k-h_n)_*\mu= P\quad \text{weakly,}     
\end{equation}
for some probability measure $P$ on $\mathbb{Z}$.
Then, if $S^f$ is the integral automorphism given by $S$ and $f$, the following convergence holds:
\[
U_{S^f}^{-h_n}\to \sum_{k\in\mathbb{Z}}P(\{k\})U_{S^f}^k,
\]
in the weak operator topology.
<!-- end theorem-3 -->
<!-- theorem-4: body_md -->
\label{thm:GHR}
Let $(X,\mu,T)$ be a $2$-simple weakly mixing system which does not have a factor whose spectrum is Lebesgue. Then $(X,\mu,T)$ is $k$-simple for every $k\ge 2$.
<!-- end theorem-4 -->
<!-- theorem-5: body_md -->
\label{thm:dJR}
    Assume that $(T,\mu)$ is simple of all orders with a trivial centralizer and $(S,\nu)$ is ergodic. If $T$ and $S$ are not disjoint, then there exists $k\in\mathbb{N}$ such that $(T^{\odot k},\mu^{\odot k})$ is a factor of $(S,\nu)$.
<!-- end theorem-5 -->
<!-- lemma-2: body_md -->
\label{lem:notlmsymmetric}
    If $(X,\mathcal B,\mu,T)$ is not lighlty mixing, then for any $k\in\mathbb{N}$, the symmetric power $T^{\odot k}$ is also not lightly mixing.
<!-- end lemma-2 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
Since $T$ is not lightly mixing, there exists a set $A\in\mathcal B$, with $\mu(A)>0$
    such that 
    \[
    \liminf_{n\to\infty}\mu(A\cap T^n B)=0.
    \]
    Then if for $C\in\{A,B\}$, we denote $C^{\odot k}:=\{\{x_1,\ldots,x_k\}\mid x_1,\ldots,x_k\in C\}$ and $C^{\times k}:=\{(x_1,\ldots,x_k)\mid x_1,\ldots,x_k\in C\}$, then
    \[
    \begin{split}
    \liminf_{n\to\infty} &\mu^{\odot k}\big(A^{\odot k}\cap (T^{\odot k})^n(B^{\odot k})\big)=\liminf_{n\to\infty} \mu^{\otimes k}\big(A^{\times k}\cap (T^{\times k})^n(B^{\times k})\big)\\
    &\le \liminf_{n\to\infty}(A\cap T^nB)=0,
    \end{split}
    \]
    which gives that $T^{\odot k}$ is not lightly mixing.
<!-- end proof-1 -->
<!-- theorem-6: body_md -->
\label{thm:FHZ}
    Every 3-IET $T$ is either 
    \begin{enumerate}
    \item rigid, or
    \item has minimal self-joinings.
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end theorem-6 -->
<!-- remark-1: body_md -->
In fact, in \cite{FHZ}, the authors proved the above dichotomy under the assumption that the IET $T$ satisfies the \emph{Keane condition} (see \cite{Keane75} for definition). However, Bernazzani in \cite{Bernazzani} proved, that if this condition is not satisfied, then the 3-IET under consideration is a finite constant suspension (,,a tower'') of a rotation, which is again, a rigid transformation.
<!-- end remark-1 -->
<!-- theorem-7: body_md -->
\label{thm:BC}
    No 3-IET is topologically mixing.
<!-- end theorem-7 -->
<!-- corollary-1: body_md -->
\label{cor:nolm}
    No 3-IET is lightly mixing.
<!-- end corollary-1 -->
<!-- proof-2: body_md -->
Let $T$ be a 3-IET. By Theorem \ref{thm:BC}, there exist two open sets $A,B\in [0,1)$ and an increasing sequence $\{n_k\}_{k\in\mathbb{N}}$ such that
    \[
    A\cap T^{n_k}B=\emptyset.
    \]
    Thus
    \[
    \liminf_{n\to\infty}Leb(A\cap T^{n}B)=0,
    \]
which shows that $T$ is not lightly mixing.
<!-- end proof-2 -->
<!-- remark-2: body_md -->
Note that, since we assume that $T$ has minimal self-joinings, it has no non-trival factors. In particular, in view of Corollary \cite{cor:nolm}, it has no lightly mixing factors. However, this is a weaker property than being disjoint from a lightly mixing system.
<!-- end remark-2 -->
